I could not find a winning sequence, and my analysis says none exists under these rules. The sequence below is my best partial attempt, and I expect it to fail.

**Why the level looks unsolvable**

- The only route from the room to the doors goes (6,6) → (6,7) → (6,8) → (5,8) → (4,8) → (3,8) → (2,8). Gate (5,8) needs goblin #8 on plate (6,11) to stay open. Gate (3,8) needs plate (2,6) pressed.
- Any hero at (6,8) dies to goblin #9 at (6,9). The only way to remove goblin #9 is dragon breath down column 6. The dragon can only be moved by pushing it to (6,2), since walls block every other push. Its breath then runs down column 6 on every move.
- The dragon breath kills goblin #9 on the first move after the push. On the next move it kills goblin #8, which unpresses (6,11) and closes gate (5,8). Nothing else can block the breath in time, because the warrior is left on (5,2) and the thief cannot reach (5,2) to pull the dragon back.
- Once the breath is gone, heroes still need both plates kept pressed. A hero standing on a plate on the room side can never leave it without closing the gate behind it. So each plate's final presser must be a non-hero. That means a crystal on (2,6) and goblin #8 alive on (6,11). Goblin #8 is killed by the breath, and there is only one crystal.

**Best attempt (expected to fail):** the warrior walks to (4,2) and pushes the dragon east, killing goblin #9.

The checker's result matches my model: all three moves were legal and the level is not won, which is expected since the moves only kill goblin #9. I still have no winning line, and my analysis says none exists under the rules as written.

The core problem is that both gates on the route to the doors need a permanent non-hero presser at the moment the last hero crosses. The only non-heroes that can reach those plates are the crystal and goblin #8. Once the dragon breath kills goblin #9, it runs down column 6 and kills goblin #8 on the next move. The warrior is stuck on (5,2) after the push, so nothing can block the breath or return the dragon in time. The crystal cannot serve both plates, because moving it from (6,11) to (2,6) would require pushing from the east side after both heroes have crossed.

Two assumptions would change this answer if they are wrong: that the breath fires on every move while the dragon sits at (6,2), and that a closed gate blocks pulls as well as walking. If your checker treats either differently, please tell me the rule and I'll re-solve.

The checker confirms that the three moves were legal, which matches my model. The obstacle is that after the dragon kills goblin #9, goblin #8 dies on the next move. That closes gate (5,8), and the only non-hero that could then hold a plate is the single crystal, which is also needed at (2,6).

If you can confirm any of these, I can re-solve: that the dragon breath fires on every move while it faces down column 6, that a closed gate also blocks pulls, or that a hero can be moved across a gate while its plate is held by another hero. Any of those being different would change the analysis.
